models.title: Surplus-optimization objective (certainty equivalent of surplus return) in decimal form
models.summary: Liability-relative objective: expected surplus return minus one-half the risk aversion coefficient times surplus-return variance, in decimals.

relationship.original_equation: UmLR = E(Rs,m) − 0.005 λ σ²(Rs,m) (percent form); = E(Rs,m) − 0.5 λ σ²(Rs,m) in decimals
relationship.locator: PDF: LM4 Surplus Optimization, printed p. 240 (PDF p. 250), Eq. 2
relationship.translation_notes: Source Eq. 2 uses 0.005 with percentage inputs (same convention as asset-only Eq. 1); record uses decimal form so the scale factor is 0.5, consistent with the source's own decimal restatement for Eq. 1. The 0.5 is a pure arithmetic scaling literal. Surplus return Rs,m = (change in asset value − change in liability value)/(initial asset value). Dimensional check: dimensionless throughout.

variables.definition: Expected surplus return for asset mix m over the horizon, in decimal form
variables.context: same asset mix m, liabilities, and horizon as UmLR

variables.definition: Investor risk aversion coefficient penalizing surplus-return volatility (same meaning as asset-only record)
variables.context: same investor and asset mix m as UmLR
variables.domain: Nonnegative finite coefficient; zero is the risk-neutral boundary

variables.definition: Surplus-return volatility (standard deviation of surplus return) for mix m, in decimal form
variables.context: same asset mix m, liabilities, and horizon as UmLR

variables.definition: Surplus objective value (certainty equivalent of surplus return) for mix m, in decimal form
variables.context: same asset mix m, liabilities, and horizon as inputs

assumptions: Surplus return is defined over the chosen horizon as asset change minus liability change per initial asset value; liability return captures time value plus expected discount-rate and cash-flow changes.
Single-period mean–variance framing applied to surplus rather than assets alone.
limitations: Same algebraic form as the asset-only utility record (batch b01) but distinct scope; see integration gaps — not a duplicate.
Correlation between assets and liabilities must be estimated (expanded matrix); estimation error is outside this record.

sources.title: The Risk Aversion Coefficient (Desjardins Online Brokerage, citing Bodie–Kane–Marcus)
sources.version: Educational article citing Investments by Bodie, Kane, Marcus, Perrakis & Ryan (2014), McGraw Hill Ryerson, 8th Canadian ed., p. 156
sources.locator: Utility formula section: U = E(r) − 0.5 × A × σ² with two worked decimal examples

sources.redistribution: Short original paraphrase and single-formula transcription only; no extended quotation

references.method: Direct substitution: 0.08 − 0.5·2·0.01 = 0.07. Independently constructed check of the decimal scaling.
references.provenance: Independent arithmetic check constructed for this record; no observed plan data claimed

references.method: Zero surplus volatility gives utility equal to expected surplus return by substitution.
references.provenance: Definitional boundary check; not an empirical validation

rejection_cases.reason: Negative risk aversion contradicts the stated penalty framing (guard lam >= 0).
Surplus-return volatility is required; expected surplus return and risk aversion alone cannot determine the objective.

models.inverse_notes: ERs = UmLR + 0.5·lam·sigS² always; lam = 2·(ERs − UmLR)/sigS² requires sigS ≠ 0; sigS = sqrt(2·(ERs − UmLR)/lam) requires lam > 0 and ERs ≥ UmLR. Substitution check: UmLR=0.07, lam=2, sigS=0.1 recovers ERs=0.08. Algebraic only.

gaps: Quantity meanings expected_surplus_return, surplus_return_volatility, surplus_utility (and shared risk_aversion_coefficient) are not in the runtime vocabulary snapshot and require extension.

Shares its algebraic form with financial-analysis--mean-variance-utility-certainty-equivalent-decimal@r1 (batch b01) but differs in scope (surplus vs asset return); recorded as a distinct model with this overlap note, not a duplicate.

models.title: Safety-first ratio (excess over threshold per unit of volatility)
models.summary: Roy's safety-first ratio: expected portfolio return minus the threshold return, divided by return volatility; higher is better under normality.

relationship.locator: PDF: LM4 Example 1 setup, printed p. 206 (PDF p. 216), ratio expression; applied printed p. 207 (PDF p. 217)
relationship.translation_notes: Decimal form (unit 1); RL is the threshold (minimum acceptable) return over the same horizon. Under a normal return assumption the ratio is the z-score-like distance whose maximization minimizes shortfall probability P(RP < RL). Dimensional check: (dimensionless − dimensionless)/dimensionless = dimensionless.

variables.definition: Expected return of the portfolio over the horizon, in decimal form (same meaning as utility record)
variables.context: same portfolio and horizon as SFR

variables.definition: Minimum acceptable (threshold) return that must be achieved, e.g. to avoid invading capital, in decimal form
variables.context: same portfolio and horizon as SFR

variables.definition: Standard deviation of portfolio return over the horizon, in decimal form
variables.context: same portfolio and horizon as SFR

variables.definition: Safety-first ratio: threshold-excess return per unit of volatility; higher means lower shortfall probability under normality
variables.context: same portfolio, threshold, and horizon as inputs

assumptions: Returns are approximately normal over the horizon, so the ratio maps to the probability of exceeding the threshold.
Threshold RL is fixed for the decision (e.g. 5% to avoid invading capital in the source example).
limitations: Under non-normal returns the ratio still ranks threshold-excess per unit volatility but no longer maps exactly to shortfall probability.
Complements, not replaces, the utility objective: allocations A and B in the source share utility 6% but differ in SFR.

rejection_cases.reason: Zero volatility makes the ratio undefined (guard sigp > 0); a risk-free payoff meeting the threshold needs no shortfall ranking.

models.inverse_notes: ERp = RL + SFR·sigp always; RL = ERp − SFR·sigp always; sigp = (ERp − RL)/SFR requires SFR ≠ 0 (zero excess with positive volatility gives SFR = 0, leaving sigp undetermined). Substitution check: SFR=0.25, RL=0.05, sigp=0.2 recovers ERp=0.10. Algebraic only; threshold choice is a preference, not an estimated quantity.

Distinct from the Sharpe ratio (risk-free rate in place of RL); do not relabel one as the other per the brief.

models.title: ARCH-family one-lag conditional variance update
models.summary: Period-t variance as a constant plus persistence-weighted prior variance plus a shock coefficient times the squared unexpected return.

relationship.original_equation: σt² = γ + α σt−1² + β ηt²
relationship.locator: PDF: LM2 Time-Varying Volatility: ARCH Models, printed p. 111 (PDF p. 121), Eq. 17
relationship.translation_notes: Source presents this as one of the simplest, heavily used forms of the ARCH class (rearranged second line shows the shock term ηt² − σt−1²). ηt is the mean-zero unexpected return component. Unconditional variance γ/(1 − α − β) is a derived identity, not separately curated. Dimensional check: variance + dimensionless×variance + dimensionless×(return²) — all variance-dimensioned in decimal-squared units.

variables.definition: Nonnegative baseline constant of the variance recursion, in decimal-variance units
variables.context: same return series and estimation as sig2t

variables.definition: Persistence weight on prior-period variance (memory/clustering strength)
variables.context: same return series and estimation as sig2t
variables.domain: Nonnegative; alpha + beta below 1 for stationarity

variables.definition: Estimated variance at time t−1, in decimal-variance units
variables.context: same return series and estimation as sig2t

variables.definition: Loading of the current squared shock onto variance
variables.context: same return series and estimation as sig2t
variables.domain: Nonnegative; alpha + beta below 1 for stationarity

variables.definition: Squared unexpected return component in period t (mean-zero shock squared), in decimal-variance units
variables.context: same return series, period t, and estimation as sig2t

variables.definition: Conditional variance in period t, in decimal-variance units
variables.context: same return series and estimation as inputs

assumptions: Parameters are nonnegative with alpha + beta below 1 (stationarity, finite unconditional variance γ/(1 − α − β)), per source.
ηt is mean-zero conditional on time t−1 information; shock sign does not matter (squared).
limitations: One-lag, single-asset form only; multi-asset VCV extensions need many more parameters (per source, Engle 2002 class handles large matrices).
Estimation of γ, α, β themselves is outside this update record.

models.inverse_notes: gam = sig2t − alpha·sig2t1 − beta·eta2t always; alpha = (sig2t − gam − beta·eta2t)/sig2t1 requires sig2t1 ≠ 0; beta = (sig2t − gam − alpha·sig2t1)/eta2t requires eta2t ≠ 0. Substitution check: sig2t=0.000434 with gam=0.000002, alpha=0.9, sig2t1=0.0004 recovers beta=0.08 given eta2t=0.0009. Algebraic only; parameter estimation is outside this record.

models.title: Risk-parity equal risk contribution condition (variance form)
models.summary: Each asset's weight times its covariance with the portfolio equals one-nth of portfolio variance.

relationship.locator: PDF: LM4 Solutions, printed p. 297 (PDF p. 307), Q7 solution
relationship.translation_notes: Record's expression is the left-hand risk contribution RCi = wi·Covi; the defining condition equates it to σp²/n, checked in references. Equivalent to the volatility-share form RCi/σp = σp/n (each asset carries 1/n of total risk): multiply through by σp. Dimensional check: dimensionless weight × variance-dimensioned covariance = variance-dimensioned contribution, compared against variance/n.

variables.definition: Fraction of portfolio money in asset i (weights sum to 1)
variables.context: same portfolio and risk parity allocation as RCi
variables.domain: Closed interval 0 to 1 inclusive for the long-only case

variables.definition: Covariance of asset i return with the portfolio return, in decimal-variance units
variables.context: same portfolio and estimation window as RCi

variables.source_symbol: introduced RCi for wi × Cov(ri, rp)
variables.definition: Asset i's total contribution to portfolio variance; equals σp²/n under risk parity
variables.context: same portfolio and estimation window as inputs
variables.domain: Nonnegative finite contribution in the long-only case

assumptions: Long-only, fully invested portfolio (weights sum to 1); contributions are nonnegative in this case.
Covariances estimated over a consistent window for all assets.
limitations: Condition defines the allocation implicitly; solving weights requires optimization (per source, constrained weights summing to 100%).
Ignores expected returns by construction (per source critique); leverage/scale to investor risk appetite is a separate step.
